statement.text: Let ''G=(S,T;E)'' be a bipartite graph, with weights <math>w:E \to [0,1]</math>. A '''proper weighted edge colouring''' is a colouring of the edges such that at each vertex, the sum of weights of edges of the same colour is at most 1. A lower bound for the number of colours is the minimum number of unit bins needed to pack the weights incident to any vertex, denoted by ''b''. Is there always a proper weighted edge colouring using <math>2b-1</math> colours?
